image.alt: Details A cardioid, with its cusp opening to the left, is graphed on the x y coordinate plane. This cardioid is symmetric about the x axis. It enters on the positive x axis, goes up and to the left, reaches its topmost point in the first quadrant, then goes down and to the left by crossing the positive y axis, reaches its leftmost point in the second quadrant, then goes down and to the right, and reaches the origin. It then enters into the third quadrant by reflecting the earlier path, goes down and to the left, again reaches its leftmost point in the third quadrant, crosses the negative y axis by falling to the right, reaches its low point in the fourth quadrant, then goes up and to the right, and ends on the positive x axis at the entry point of the cardioid. A solid dot is marked on the cardioid on the positive y axis.

Details A function with two parts is graphed on the x y coordinate plane. The first part lies entirely above the x axis and is symmetric about the y axis. It enters the second quadrant above the negative x axis, goes up and to the right, concave up, veering away from the x axis, then becomes concave down, reaches its high point on the positive y axis, goes down and to the right, passes through a marked solid dot, then becomes concave up, and veers toward the x axis as the curve proceeds rightward. The second part lies entirely below the x axis and is symmetric about the y axis. It enters the third quadrant below the x axis, goes down and to the right as it veers away from the x axis, concave down, crosses the negative y axis, enters into the fourth quadrant, then falls to the left, again reaches the negative y axis. It then re-enters into the third quadrant by rising to the right, again crossing the negative y axis such that it forms a loop on the negative y axis. It then continues to rise to the right, concave down, and approaches the x axis as the curve veers toward it.

Details A closed curve is graphed on the x y coordinate plane. The closed curve resembles the infinity symbol and is symmetric about the origin. The curve enters at the origin, goes down and to the left in the third quadrant, concave up, reaches its low point, then goes steeply to the left until it reaches the negative x axis. The curve then goes up and to the right in the second quadrant, concave down to reach its high point, then goes gradually down and to the right through the origin, thus forming a loop to the left of the y axis. The curve then goes down and to the right in the fourth quadrant, concave up, reaches its low point, then rises steeply to the right until it reaches the positive x axis. It then goes up and to the left in the first quadrant through a solid dot, concave down, reaches its high point, and then goes gradually downward to the left to the origin, thus forming another loop to the right of the y axis.

Details A function is graphed on the x y coordinate plane. The function has three parts. The first part enters the second quadrant at the top left, goes down and to the right, reaches its rightmost point in the second quadrant, then goes down and bends to the left, and reaches its leftmost point on the negative x axis. It then goes down and to the right in the third quadrant while bending rightward, and then falls to the left, mirroring its earlier path. The second part resembles a number 8-shape and is symmetric about the origin. It enters at the origin, goes up and to the right in the first quadrant, then turns leftward, crosses the y axis at its high point, then goes down and to the left in the second quadrant, and reaches the origin. It then goes down and to the right into the fourth quadrant, turns leftward, reaches its low point on the negative y axis, enters into the third quadrant, and then gradually goes up and to the right, and reaches the origin. A solid dot is marked on the negative y axis at the low point of the curve. The third part is the mirror image of the first part such that it enters the viewing window in the first quadrant, reaches its leftmost in the second quadrant and the fourth quadrant, and the rightmost point on the positive x axis.

list.item: The curve with equation $$y^{2} = 5x^{4} - x^{2}$$ is called a kampyle of Eudoxus. Find an equation of the tangent line to this curve at the point $$\left( {1,2} \right)$$ .
Illustrate part (a) by graphing the curve and the tangent line on a common screen. (Graph the implicitly defined curve if possible, or you can graph the upper and lower halves separately.)
The curve with equation $$y^{2} = x^{3} + 3x^{2}$$ is called the Tschirnhausen cubic. Find an equation of the tangent line to this curve at the point $$\left( {1, - 2} \right)$$ .
At what points does this curve have horizontal tangents?
Illustrate parts (a) and (b) by graphing the curve and the tangent lines on a common screen.

exercises.paragraph: 53, 54, 55, and 56 Orthogonal Trajectories Two curves are orthogonal if their tangent lines are perpendicular at each point of intersection. Show that the given families of curves are orthogonal trajectories of each other; that is, every curve in one family is orthogonal to every curve in the other family. Sketch both families of curves on the same axes.

problem.paragraph: Show that the ellipse $$x^{2} \slash a^{2} + y^{2} \slash b^{2} = 1$$ and the hyperbola $$x^{2} \slash A^{2} - y^{2} \slash B^{2} = 1$$ are orthogonal trajectories if $$A^{2} < a^{2}$$ and $$a^{2} - b^{2} = A^{2} + B^{2}$$ (so the ellipse and hyperbola have the same foci).
Find the value of the number $$a$$ such that the families of curves $$y = \left( {x + c} \right)^{- 1}$$ and $$y = a\left( {x + k} \right)^{1 \slash 3}$$ are orthogonal trajectories.

problem.paragraph: The figure shows a lamp located three units to the right of the $$y$$ -axis and a shadow created by the elliptical region $$x^{2} + 4y^{2} \leqslant 5$$ . If the point $$\left( {- 5,0} \right)$$ is on the edge of the shadow, how far above the $$x$$ -axis is the lamp located?

image.alt: Details A street lamp post is superimposed on the x y coordinate plane. The x axis is displayed from negative 5 to 3. The lamp post stands on the right of the tick mark 3, and the head of the lamp lies directly above the tick mark 3. The shadow of the lamp creates a horizontal elliptical region labeled x^2 + 4 y^2 = 5 with center (0, 0). From the head of the lamp, two dashed lines are drawn: one goes down and to the left by crossing the positive y axis, touches the ellipse in the second quadrant, and again crosses the x axis at (negative 5, 0); the other goes down and to the left, steeper than the first one, touches the ellipse near the positive x axis, and extends in the fourth quadrant. The vertical distance from the x axis to the head of the lamp is labeled question mark.
